newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon to seek more U.S. base closings.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon to seek more U.S. base closings.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Cohen will seek the closing of more military bases in the United States in a major U.S. defense strategy review to be sent to Congress this month, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

The Quadrennial Defense Review (QDR) will also seek at least $1 billion in additional spending on developing a national defense against missile attack, Defense Department spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters.

"He will seek additional base closures," Bacon said, confirming strong hints from Cohen in recent weeks that more bases must be closed to catch up with deep cuts in U.S. military forces since the end of the Cold War.
The Pentagon has shut down dozens of big domestic bases and hundreds of smaller facilities in four rounds of base closings scheduled to be completed in 2001.

Defense officials, who asked not to be identified, said Cohen intended to press lawmakers to approve an additional two rounds of politically-touchy domestic base closings, one in 1999 and the other in 2001. Such closings are a problem for many communities, which depend on military payrolls and purchasing power.

Bacon said the QDR would recommend additional spending of between $1 billion and $2 billion to prepare technology for a potential national missile defense by 1999 in case the Pentagon decides then that such a system should be deployed by the year 2003.
